title: Parse free-text data using systematic keyword extraction and synonym merging
when_to_use: When analyzing job descriptions, product reviews, or any free-text field for structured insights.
experience:
- **Extract from all relevant text columns**: Don't rely only on dedicated columns (e.g., 'Benefits'); also parse longer free-text fields (e.g., 'Job Description') using keyword lists or NLP.
- **Build a unified synonym dictionary**: Create a mapping to merge equivalent terms (e.g., 'high-temperature allowance' ↔ 'high temperature allowance') before counting.
- **Normalize multi‑level categories**: Group extracted terms into broader categories (e.g., 'Technical Skills', 'Soft Skills') using a hierarchical dictionary.
- **Validate coverage**: Compare counts from raw‑field extraction versus full‑text extraction to ensure completeness.
- **Report method**: Explicitly state which columns were used for extraction and how synonyms were merged.
checklist: Extract from all text columns that may contain relevant info
Build and apply a synonym dictionary to merge equivalent terms
Group terms into meaningful categories if the task requires categorization
Cross‑validate extraction by comparing counts across methods
common_failure_prevented: Missing significant portions of relevant data because the analysis only considered structured columns and ignored free‑text fields.

title: Define comprehensive analysis dimensions from task keywords before diving into data
when_to_use: When the task asks for 'qualities', 'factors', 'characteristics', or 'dimensions' that influence an outcome.
experience:
- **Brainstorm a dimension map**: Before querying, list all possible dimensions suggested by the task (e.g., for 'qualities increasing salary': years of experience, language skills, certifications, industry, company type, soft skills, technical skills).
- **Map dimensions to data columns**: Identify which columns or text fields contain each dimension; note if some dimensions require parsing free‑text.
- **Plan extraction for each dimension**: Design specific methods for each (e.g., regex for years, keyword lists for skills, categorical mapping for industries).
- **Prioritize by data coverage**: Start with dimensions that have sufficient data and clear definitions.
- **Document missing dimensions**: Explicitly note if any brainstormed dimension cannot be extracted due to data limitations.
checklist: Brainstorm a comprehensive list of analysis dimensions from the task statement
Map each dimension to specific data columns or free‑text fields
Design extraction methods for each dimension, especially those requiring text parsing
Note any dimensions that cannot be analyzed due to data constraints
common_failure_prevented: Overlooking major categories of influencing factors because the analysis focused only on a few obvious structured columns.

title: Cross‑validate data‑parsing outputs against known distributions or sample checks
when_to_use: When extracting numerical values or categories from semi‑structured text (e.g., salary ranges, date ranges, coded fields).
experience:
- **Create a validation sample**: Randomly sample 50–100 raw text entries and manually extract the target values.
- **Compare automated vs. manual results**: Calculate error rates (e.g., percentage of mismatches) for key fields.
- **Refine parsing logic iteratively**: Use mismatches to improve regex patterns or handling of edge cases (e.g., commission‑based salaries, unit variations).
- **Check distribution reasonableness**: Compare the automated distribution (e.g., salary bins) to industry benchmarks or simple heuristics (e.g., minimum wage).
- **Report parsing accuracy**: In the final analysis, state the estimated accuracy of extraction based on the validation sample.
checklist: Manually extract a random sample of raw text to create a ground‑truth set
Compare automated extraction against the manual set to quantify errors
Iteratively improve parsing rules based on observed mismatches
Compare the overall distribution to external benchmarks or common sense
common_failure_prevented: Reporting significantly inaccurate distributions due to unvalidated parsing logic (e.g., salary bin errors >20%).
